title.zh: 卷52 列傳第17 韓擒虎 賀若弼
title.en: Volume 52 Biographies 17: Han Qinhu, He Ruobi
title.raw: 卷52 列傳第17 韓擒虎 賀若弼 Volume 52 Biographies 17: Han Qinhu, He Ruobi

sentences.zh: 隋書卷五十二列傳第十七

translations.literal: Book of Sui, fascicle fifty-two, Biographies section seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 52, Biographies 17

sentences.zh: ○韓擒虎弟僧壽洪

translations.literal: ○ Han Qinhu; his younger brothers Shengshou and Hong.
translations.idiomatic: ○ Han Qinhu; his younger brothers Shengshou and Hong

sentences.zh: 韓擒虎，字子通，河南東垣人也，後家新安。

translations.literal: Han Qinhu, courtesy name Zitong, was a native of Dongyuan in Henan; his family later settled in Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qinhu, whose courtesy name was Zitong, came from Dongyuan in Henan; his household later moved to Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 父雄，以武烈知名，仕周，官至大將軍、洛虞等八州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xiong was famed for martial valor, served the Zhou, and rose to Grand General and governor of eight prefectures including Luo and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiong was renowned for martial prowess, served the Northern Zhou, and rose to Grand General and governor of eight prefectures, among them Luo and Yu.

sentences.zh: 擒虎少慷慨，以膽略見稱，容貌魁岸，有雄傑之表。

translations.literal: Qinhu from youth was generous-spirited, renowned for courage and stratagem, tall and imposing in appearance, with the bearing of a heroic figure.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Qinhu was open-handed and bold, famed for courage and strategy; he was tall and imposing, with the bearing of a great hero.

sentences.zh: 性又好書，經史百家皆略知大旨。

translations.literal: By nature he also loved books and had a general grasp of the essential points of the classics, histories, and the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved learning by nature and had a working grasp of the main themes of the classics, histories, and the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 周太祖見而異之，令與諸子遊集。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu of Zhou saw him as extraordinary and had him join in the princes' gatherings for companionship.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu of the Northern Zhou noticed him as exceptional and had him keep company with the imperial sons.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功，拜都督、新安太守，稍遷儀同三司，襲爵新義郡公。

translations.literal: Later for military merit he was appointed Commissioner-in-Chief and Administrator of Xin'an, gradually rose to Senior General-in-Chief of the Third Rank, and inherited the title Duke of Xinyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for military merit, he was made Commissioner-in-Chief and Administrator of Xin'an, gradually advanced to Senior General-in-Chief of the Third Rank, and inherited the title Duke of Xinyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 武帝伐齊，齊將獨孤永業守金墉城，擒虎說下之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu attacked Qi, the Qi general Dugu Yongye held Jinyong city; Qinhu persuaded him to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu campaigned against Northern Qi, the Qi general Dugu Yongye held Jinyong; Qinhu talked him into surrendering.

sentences.zh: 進平范陽，加上儀同，拜永州刺史。

translations.literal: Advancing to pacify Fanyang, he was given the added title Senior General-in-Chief and appointed Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to pacify Fanyang, was given the added rank of Senior General-in-Chief, and was appointed Governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 陳人逼光州，擒虎以行軍總管擊破之。

translations.literal: When Chen forces pressed Guangzhou, Qinhu as campaigning commander-in-chief defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen forces threatened Guangzhou, Qinhu, serving as campaigning commander-in-chief, routed them.

sentences.zh: 又從宇文忻平合州。

translations.literal: He also followed Yuwen Xin in pacifying He prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Yuwen Xin in pacifying He prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，遷和州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu served as Chancellor, Qinhu was transferred to Governor of He prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu was serving as Chancellor, Qinhu was transferred to Governor of He prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陳將甄慶、任蠻奴、蕭摩訶等共為聲援，頻寇江北，前後入界。

translations.literal: The Chen generals Zhen Qing, Ren Mannu, Xiao Mohe and others jointly supported one another militarily, repeatedly raiding north of the Yangzi and crossing the border time after time.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen generals Zhen Qing, Ren Mannu, Xiao Mohe, and others backed one another in force, raiding the north bank of the Yangzi again and again and crossing the border repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 擒虎屢挫其鋒，陳人奪氣。

translations.literal: Qinhu repeatedly blunted their offensive, and the Chen troops lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Qinhu repeatedly broke their momentum, and the Chen troops lost their fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，高祖潛有吞併江南之志，以擒虎有文武才用，夙著聲名，於是拜為廬州總管，委以平陳之任，甚為敵人所憚。

translations.literal: Early in the Kaihuang era, Emperor Gaozu secretly harbored the aim of annexing the Jiangnan region; because Qinhu combined civil and military talent and had long been famed, he was appointed Chief Administrator of Luzhou and entrusted with the task of pacifying Chen, greatly feared by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang reign, Emperor Gaozu secretly intended to annex the south; because Qinhu possessed both civil and military gifts and had long been famous, he was appointed Chief Administrator of Luzhou and entrusted with the conquest of Chen—a man greatly feared by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 及大舉伐陳，以擒虎為先鋒。

translations.literal: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, Qinhu was made vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, Qinhu was made vanguard.

sentences.zh: 擒虎率五百人宵濟，襲採石，守者皆醉，擒虎遂取之。

translations.literal: Qinhu led five hundred men across by night, stormed Caishi, the defenders were all drunk, and Qinhu took it.
translations.idiomatic: Qinhu led five hundred men across the river by night, struck Caishi, found the garrison drunk, and took the place.

sentences.zh: 進攻姑熟，半日而拔，次於新林。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Gushu, took it in half a day, and made camp at Xinlin.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to Gushu, captured it in half a day, and encamped at Xinlin.

sentences.zh: 江南父老素聞其威信，來謁軍門，晝夜不絕。

translations.literal: Elders of the Jiangnan region had long heard of his prestige and trustworthiness; they came to pay respects at his camp gates without cease day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The elders of Jiangnan had long heard of his prestige; they came to his camp day and night without end.

sentences.zh: 陳人大駭，其將樊巡、魯世真、田瑞等相繼降之。

translations.literal: The Chen people were greatly alarmed; their generals Fan Xun, Lu Shizhen, Tian Rui and others surrendered to him one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen were thrown into panic; their generals Fan Xun, Lu Shizhen, Tian Rui, and others surrendered to him in succession.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣上狀，高祖聞而大悅，宴賜群臣。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang reported in a memorial; the emperor heard and was greatly pleased, and held a feast to reward the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, sent a report; the emperor was greatly pleased and held a feast to reward his ministers.

sentences.zh: 晉王遣行軍總管杜彥與擒虎合軍，步騎二萬，陳叔寶遣領軍蔡徵守朱雀航，聞擒虎將至，眾懼而潰。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin sent campaigning commander-in-chief Du Yan to join forces with Qinhu—twenty thousand foot and horse; Chen Shubao sent Commandant-in-Chief Cai Zheng to hold Zhuque crossing; hearing Qinhu was approaching, the troops were afraid and fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin sent the campaigning commander-in-chief Du Yan to join Qinhu with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry. Chen Shubao sent the Commandant-in-Chief Cai Zheng to hold Zhuque Ford; when the troops heard Qinhu was coming, they panicked and broke.

sentences.zh: 任蠻奴為賀若弼所敗，棄軍降於擒虎。

translations.literal: Ren Mannu was defeated by He Ruobi, abandoned his army and surrendered to Qinhu.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Mannu was defeated by He Ruobi, abandoned his army, and surrendered to Qinhu.

sentences.zh: 擒虎以精騎五百，直入硃雀門。

translations.literal: Qinhu with five hundred crack horsemen entered straight through the Zhuque Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Qinhu entered the Zhuque Gate at the head of five hundred picked horsemen.

sentences.zh: 陳人欲戰，蠻奴捴之曰：「老夫尚降，諸君何事！

translations.literal: The Chen men wished to fight; Mannu seized them and said: "This old man has already surrendered—what business have you lot!
translations.idiomatic: The Chen troops wanted to fight, but Mannu seized them and cried, "This old man has already surrendered—what are you still fighting for!

sentences.zh: 」眾皆散走。

translations.literal: " The crowd all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: " The men all scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 遂平金陵，執陳主叔寶。

translations.literal: He thus pacified Jinling and seized Chen ruler Shubao.
translations.idiomatic: He then pacified Jinling and seized the Chen ruler, Shubao.

sentences.zh: 時賀若弼亦有功。

translations.literal: At that time He Ruobi also had merit.
translations.idiomatic: At that time He Ruobi had merit as well.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔于晉王曰：「此二公者，深謀大略，東南逋寇，朕本委之，靜地恤民，悉如朕意。

translations.literal: The emperor then issued an edict to the Prince of Jin saying: "These two lords possess deep strategy and grand design; the fugitive rebels of the southeast—I originally entrusted them to bring quiet to the land and care for the people, and all has been as I wished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict to the Prince of Jin: "These two men possess deep strategy and grand design. The fugitive rebels of the southeast—I originally entrusted them with pacifying the land and caring for the people, and all has gone as I wished.

sentences.zh: 九州不一，已數百年，以名臣之功，成太平之業，天下盛事，何用過此！

translations.literal: The Nine Provinces have not been united for several hundred years; through the merit of famed ministers to accomplish the work of great peace—what event under heaven could surpass this!
translations.idiomatic: The realm has been divided for centuries; through the merit of famed ministers a work of great peace has been achieved. What event under heaven could surpass this!

sentences.zh: 聞以欣然，實深慶快。

translations.literal: Upon hearing it I am pleased with joy; truly I am deeply gratified.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this fills me with joy; I am deeply gratified indeed.

sentences.zh: 平定江表，二人之力也。

translations.literal: Pacifying the Jiangbiao region is the work of these two men.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification of the lower Yangzi is the achievement of these two men.

sentences.zh: 」賜物萬段。

translations.literal: " He bestowed ten thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: " He bestowed ten thousand lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 又下優詔於擒虎、弼曰：「申國威于萬里，宣朝化於一隅，使東南之民俱出湯火，數百年寇旬日廓清，專是公之功也。

translations.literal: He also issued a gracious edict to Qinhu and Bi saying: "You have displayed the state's prestige over ten thousand li, spread the court's transforming influence in one corner, lifted the people of the southeast all out of boiling water and raging fire; centuries of raiders were cleared in a matter of days—this is entirely your merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also issued a gracious edict to Qinhu and Bi: "You have displayed the state's might across ten thousand li and spread the court's transforming influence in one corner, lifting the people of the southeast out of fire and flood. Raiders that had troubled the land for centuries were cleared in a matter of days—this is entirely your achievement.

sentences.zh: 高名塞于宇宙，盛業光於天壤，逖聽前古，罕聞其匹。

translations.literal: Your lofty fame fills heaven and earth, your splendid achievement shines across the realm; listening back through former ages, one rarely hears your equal.
translations.idiomatic: Your lofty fame fills heaven and earth; your splendid achievement shines across the realm. Listening back through former ages, one rarely hears your equal.

sentences.zh: 班師凱入，誠知非遠，相思之甚，寸陰若歲。

translations.literal: Your triumphant return is truly not far; I miss you so deeply that each inch of shadow is like a year.
translations.idiomatic: Your triumphant return cannot be far off; I miss you so deeply that each passing moment feels like a year.

sentences.zh: 」及至京，弼與擒虎爭功於上前，弼曰：「臣在蔣山死戰，破其銳卒，擒其驍將，震揚威武，遂平陳國。

translations.literal: " When they reached the capital, Bi and Qinhu contended for merit before the emperor. Bi said: "Your servant fought to the death at Jiangshan, broke their elite troops, captured their fierce generals, displayed awesome might, and thus pacified the Chen state.
translations.idiomatic: " When they reached the capital, Bi and Qinhu disputed their merits before the throne. Bi said, "Your servant fought to the death at Mount Jiang, broke their elite troops, captured their fierce generals, displayed our awesome might, and thus pacified the Chen state.

sentences.zh: 韓擒虎略不交陣，豈臣之比！

translations.literal: Han Qinhu barely engaged in battle at all—how can he compare with your servant!
translations.idiomatic: Han Qinhu barely crossed swords with the enemy—how can he compare with your servant!

sentences.zh: 」擒虎曰：「本奉明旨，令臣與弼同時合勢，以取偽都。

translations.literal: " Qinhu said: "I originally received your clear mandate that your servant and Bi should combine forces at the same time to take the false capital.
translations.idiomatic: " Qinhu said, "I originally received your clear command that your servant and Bi should combine our forces at the same time to take the rebel capital.

sentences.zh: 弼乃敢先期，逢賊遂戰，致令將士傷死甚多。

translations.literal: Bi dared to go ahead of schedule, encountered the enemy and fought, causing many officers and soldiers to be wounded and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Bi dared to move ahead of schedule, met the enemy, and fought, causing many officers and soldiers to be wounded or killed.

sentences.zh: 臣以輕騎五百，兵不血刃，直取金陵，降任蠻奴，執陳叔寶，據其府庫，傾其巢穴。

translations.literal: Your servant with five hundred light horsemen, blades unstained with blood, took Jinling straight away, made Ren Mannu surrender, seized Chen Shubao, occupied their treasuries and emptied their nest.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, with five hundred light horsemen and blades unstained with blood, took Jinling straightaway, made Ren Mannu surrender, seized Chen Shubao, seized their treasuries, and overturned their nest.

sentences.zh: 弼至夕，方扣北掖門，臣啟關而納之。

translations.literal: Bi did not come until evening before knocking at the North Side Gate; your servant opened the gate and admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: Bi did not arrive until evening, when he knocked at the North Side Gate; your servant opened the gate and let him in.

sentences.zh: 斯乃救罪不暇，安得與臣相比！

translations.literal: He can scarcely spare time to save himself from guilt—how can he compare with your servant!
translations.idiomatic: He can scarcely spare time to save himself from blame—how can he compare with your servant!

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「二將俱合上勳。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Both generals alike merit a supreme merit citation.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Both generals alike merit the highest grade of merit.

sentences.zh: 」於是進位上柱國，賜物八千段。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they were advanced to Supreme Pillar of State and bestowed eight thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon they were advanced to Supreme Pillar of State and bestowed eight thousand lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 有司劾擒虎放縱士卒，淫汙陳宮，坐此不加爵邑。

translations.literal: The relevant offices impeached Qinhu for letting his troops run wild and defiling the Chen palace; on this account he was not given added enfeoffment or fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices impeached Qinhu for letting his troops run wild and defiling the Chen palace; on that account he received no added enfeoffment or fief.

sentences.zh: 先是，江東有謠歌曰：「黃斑青驄馬，發自壽陽涘。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Jiangdong there was a ballad that said: "Yellow-spotted piebald, blue-gray steed, setting out from the banks of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Jiangdong there was a ballad: "A piebald with yellow spots, a blue-gray steed, setting out from the banks of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 來時冬氣末，去日春風始。

translations.literal: Coming when winter's breath was ending, going when spring winds began.
translations.idiomatic: It came as winter was ending; it went as spring winds were rising.

sentences.zh: 」皆不知所謂。

translations.literal: " No one knew what it meant.
translations.idiomatic: " No one knew what it meant.

sentences.zh: 擒虎本名豹，平陳之際，又乘青驄馬，往反時節與歌相應，至是方悟。

translations.literal: Qinhu's original name was Bao; at the time of pacifying Chen he again rode a blue-gray steed; the round trip matched the seasons in the song—in that moment they understood.
translations.idiomatic: Qinhu's original name was Bao; during the pacification of Chen he again rode a blue-gray steed, and the seasons of his coming and going matched the song—only then did they understand.

sentences.zh: 其後突厥來朝，上謂之曰：「汝聞江南有陳國天子乎？

translations.literal: Later when the Turks came to court, the emperor said to them: "Have you heard that in Jiangnan there was a Son of Heaven of the Chen state?
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Turks came to court, the emperor said to them, "Have you heard that in Jiangnan there was a Son of Heaven of the Chen state?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「聞之。

translations.literal: " They replied: "We have heard.
translations.idiomatic: " They replied, "We have heard.

sentences.zh: 」上命左右引突厥詣擒虎前，曰：「此是執得陳國天子者。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered attendants to lead the Turks before Qinhu and said: "This is the man who captured the Son of Heaven of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered his attendants to lead the Turks before Qinhu and said, "This is the man who captured the Son of Heaven of Chen.

sentences.zh: 」擒虎厲然顧之，突厥惶恐，不敢仰視，其有威容如此。

translations.literal: " Qinhu glared fiercely at them; the Turks were terrified and dared not look up—such was his august bearing.
translations.idiomatic: " Qinhu glared fiercely at them; the Turks were terrified and dared not look up—such was his imposing bearing.

sentences.zh: 別封壽光縣公，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Shouguang county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Shouguang county with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 以行軍總管屯金城，禦備胡寇，即拜涼州總管。

translations.literal: As campaigning commander-in-chief he was stationed at Jincheng to guard against barbarian raiders, and was appointed Chief Administrator of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As campaigning commander-in-chief he was stationed at Jincheng to guard against barbarian raiders and was appointed Chief Administrator of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄征還京，上宴之內殿，恩禮殊厚。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned back to the capital; the emperor feasted him in the inner hall with especially generous favor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned back to the capital; the emperor feasted him in the inner hall with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 無何，其鄰母見擒虎門下儀衛甚盛，有同王者，母異而問之。

translations.literal: Before long a neighbor woman saw beneath Qinhu's gate ceremonial guards as numerous as for a king; surprised, his mother asked about it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a neighbor woman saw at Qinhu's gate ceremonial guards as splendid as for a king; startled, his mother asked what it meant.

sentences.zh: 其中人曰：「我來迎王。

translations.literal: One among them said: "I have come to welcome the king.
translations.idiomatic: One among them said, "I have come to welcome the king.

sentences.zh: 」忽然不見。

translations.literal: " Suddenly they vanished.
translations.idiomatic: " Suddenly they vanished.

sentences.zh: 又有人疾篤，忽驚走至擒虎家曰：「我欲謁王。

translations.literal: Another man, gravely ill, suddenly ran in alarm to Qinhu's house and said: "I wish to pay respects to the king.
translations.idiomatic: Another man, gravely ill, suddenly ran in alarm to Qinhu's house and said, "I wish to pay my respects to the king.

sentences.zh: 」左右問曰：「何王也？

translations.literal: " Attendants asked: "Which king?
translations.idiomatic: " His attendants asked, "Which king?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「閻羅王。

translations.literal: " He answered: "King Yama.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "King Yama.

sentences.zh: 」擒虎子弟欲撻之，擒虎止之曰：「生為上柱國，死作閻羅王，斯亦足矣。

translations.literal: " Qinhu's sons and nephews wished to flog him; Qinhu stopped them and said: "Alive as Supreme Pillar of State, dead as King Yama—that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: " Qinhu's sons and nephews wished to beat him, but Qinhu stopped them and said, "Alive as Supreme Pillar of State, dead as King Yama—that is enough.

sentences.zh: 」因寢疾，數日竟卒，時年五十五。

translations.literal: " He then took to his bed with illness and after several days died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: " He then took to his bed with illness and after several days died, at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 子世諤嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shiyu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiyu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 世諤倜儻驍捷，有父風。

translations.literal: Shiyu was bold and dashing, swift in combat, with his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyu was bold and dashing, swift in battle, and had his father's manner.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之作亂也，引世諤為將，每戰先登。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan raised rebellion, he recruited Shiyu as a general; in every battle Shiyu led the charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, he recruited Shiyu as a general; in every battle Shiyu led the charge.

sentences.zh: 及玄感敗，為吏所拘。

translations.literal: When Xuangan was defeated, he was seized by officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan was defeated, Shiyu was seized by the authorities.

sentences.zh: 時帝在高陽，送詣行所。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Gaoyang; Shiyu was sent to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at Gaoyang; Shiyu was sent to the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 世諤曰令守者市酒殽以酣暢，揚言曰：「吾死在朝夕，不醉何為！

translations.literal: Shiyu got the guards to buy wine and delicacies for a merry feast, and proclaimed loudly: "My death is any day now—if not drunk, what's the use!
translations.idiomatic: Shiyu had the guards buy wine and food for a merry feast and proclaimed loudly, "I shall die any day now—if I do not get drunk, what is the use!

sentences.zh: 」漸以酒進守者，守者狎之，遂飲令致醉。

translations.literal: " Gradually he offered wine to the guards; they grew familiar, drank together and were made drunk.
translations.idiomatic: " Gradually he offered wine to the guards; they grew familiar with him, drank together, and were made drunk.

sentences.zh: 世諤因得逃奔山賊，不知所終。

translations.literal: Shiyu thus escaped to mountain bandits; his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyu thus escaped to the mountain bandits; his end is unknown.

sentences.zh: 僧壽字玄慶，擒虎母弟也，亦以勇烈知名。

translations.literal: Shengshou, courtesy name Xuanqing, was Qinhu's younger brother by the same mother and was also famed for fierce valor.
translations.idiomatic: Shengshou, whose courtesy name was Xuanqing, was Qinhu's younger brother by the same mother and was likewise famed for fierce valor.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，為侍伯中旅下大夫。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu of Zhou's time he served as Junior Grand Master of the Central Brigade of Personal Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou he served as Junior Grand Master of the Central Brigade of Personal Attendants.

sentences.zh: 高祖得政，從韋孝寬平尉迥，每戰有功，授大將軍，封昌樂公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu took power, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Yuwen Yong's rebellion; in every battle he had merit, was appointed Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Changle with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu seized power, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Yuwen Yong's rebellion; in every battle he distinguished himself, was appointed Grand General, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Changle with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，拜安州刺史。

translations.literal: Early in Kaihuang he was appointed Governor of An prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang reign he was appointed Governor of An prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時擒虎為廬州總管，朝廷不欲同在淮南，轉為熊州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Qinhu was Chief Administrator of Luzhou; the court did not wish them both in Huainan, so he was transferred to Governor of Xiong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qinhu was Chief Administrator of Luzhou; the court did not wish both brothers in Huainan, so Shengshou was transferred to Governor of Xiong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後轉蔚州刺史，進爵廣陵郡公。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Governor of Yu prefecture and advanced in rank to Duke of Guangling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to Governor of Yu prefecture and advanced in rank to Duke of Guangling commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋以行軍總管擊突厥于雞頭山，破之。

translations.literal: Soon as campaigning commander-in-chief he attacked the Turks at Mount Jitou and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as campaigning commander-in-chief, he attacked the Turks at Mount Jitou and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 後坐事免。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 數歲，複拜蔚州刺史。

translations.literal: Several years later he was again appointed Governor of Yu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was again appointed Governor of Yu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 突厥甚憚之。

translations.literal: The Turks greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 十七年，屯蘭州以備胡。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was stationed at Lanzhou to guard against the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was stationed at Lanzhou to guard against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 明年，遼東之役，領行軍總管，還，檢校靈州總管事。

translations.literal: The next year, in the Liaodong campaign, he served as campaigning commander-in-chief; on return he was made acting Chief Administrator of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, during the Liaodong campaign, he served as campaigning commander-in-chief; on his return he was made acting Chief Administrator of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 從楊素擊突厥，破之，進位上柱國，改封江都郡公。

translations.literal: Following Yang Su he attacked the Turks, defeated them, was advanced to Supreme Pillar of State, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Jiangdu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Following Yang Su he attacked the Turks and defeated them; he was advanced to Supreme Pillar of State and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Jiangdu commandery.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，又改封新蔡郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, he was again re-enfeoffed as Duke of Xincai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang acceded, he was again re-enfeoffed as Duke of Xincai commandery.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，不復任用。

translations.literal: From that time forward he was no longer employed.
translations.idiomatic: From that time forward he was no longer employed.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，從幸太原。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye he accompanied the emperor to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daye he accompanied the emperor to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 有京兆人達奚通妾王氏，能清歌，朝臣多相會觀之，僧壽亦豫焉，坐是除名。

translations.literal: A concubine of Daxi Tong of Jingzhao, the Lady Wang, could sing clear songs; many court officials gathered to watch; Shengshou also attended, and on that account was stripped of his post.
translations.idiomatic: A concubine of Daxi Tong of Jingzhao, the Lady Wang, could sing beautifully; many court officials gathered to watch her perform, and Shengshou attended as well; on that account he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 尋令復位。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered restored to office.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒于京師，時年六十五。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died in the capital, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died in the capital, at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 有子孝基。

translations.literal: He had a son Xiaoji.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Xiaoji.

sentences.zh: 洪字叔明，擒虎季弟也。

translations.literal: Hong, courtesy name Shuming, was Qinhu's youngest brother.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, whose courtesy name was Shuming, was Qinhu's youngest brother.

sentences.zh: 少驍勇，善射，膂力過人。

translations.literal: From youth he was fierce and brave, skilled at archery, with physical strength surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was fierce and brave, skilled at archery, and possessed strength beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 仕周侍伯上士，後以軍功拜大都督。

translations.literal: He served the Zhou as a senior sergeant of personal attendants, later for military merit was appointed Grand Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Northern Zhou as a senior sergeant of personal attendants and later, for military merit, was appointed Grand Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，從韋孝寬破尉迥於相州，加上開府，甘棠縣侯，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was Chancellor, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in defeating Yuwen Yong at Xiang prefecture, was given the added office Opening the Mansion, enfeoffed as Marquis of Gantang county with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu was Chancellor, Hong followed Wei Xiaokuan in defeating Yuwen Yong at Xiang prefecture, was given the added office Opening the Mansion, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gantang county with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, Hong was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, Hong was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 尋授驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 開皇九年，平陳之役，授行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaihuang, in the campaign to pacify Chen, he was appointed campaigning commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaihuang, during the campaign to pacify Chen, he was appointed campaigning commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，晉王廣大獵于蔣山，有猛獸在圍中，眾皆懼。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, the Prince of Jin Yang Guang held a great hunt at Mount Jiang; a fierce beast was within the encirclement and all were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was pacified, the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, held a great hunt on Mount Jiang; a fierce beast was trapped within the beat, and everyone was afraid.

sentences.zh: 洪馳馬射之，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Hong galloped and shot it; it fell at the twang of the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: Hong galloped up and shot it; the beast fell at the twang of his bowstring.

sentences.zh: 陳氏諸將，列觀於側，莫不歎伏焉。

translations.literal: Chen generals lined up watching from the side, all sighing in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen generals stood in ranks at the side watching; none failed to sigh in admiration.

sentences.zh: 王大喜，賜縑百匹。

translations.literal: The prince was greatly pleased and bestowed a hundred lengths of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was greatly pleased and bestowed a hundred lengths of silk.

sentences.zh: 尋以功加柱國，拜蔣州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon for merit he was made Pillar of State and appointed Governor of Jiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for his merit, he was made Pillar of State and appointed Governor of Jiang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 數歲，轉廉州刺史。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to Governor of Lian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was transferred to Governor of Lian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時突厥屢為邊患，朝廷以洪驍勇，檢校朔州總管事。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks frequently troubled the borders; the court because of Hong's valor made him acting Chief Administrator of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Turks repeatedly raided the frontier; because of Hong's valor the court made him acting Chief Administrator of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 尋拜代州總管。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Chief Administrator of Dai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Chief Administrator of Dai prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仁壽元年，突厥達頭可汗犯塞，洪率蔚州刺史劉隆、大將軍李藥王拒之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renshou, the Turkic qaghan Datou invaded the frontier; Hong led Yu Governor Liu Long and Grand General Li Yaowang to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Renshou, the Turkic qaghan Datou invaded the frontier; Hong led the Governor of Yu, Liu Long, and Grand General Li Yaowang to resist him.

sentences.zh: 遇虜于恆安，眾寡不敵，洪四面搏戰，身被重創，將士沮氣。

translations.literal: They met the enemy at Heng'an; greatly outnumbered, Hong fought on all sides, suffered grave wounds, and the troops' morale sank.
translations.idiomatic: They met the enemy at Heng'an; greatly outnumbered, Hong fought on every side, suffered grave wounds, and his troops' spirits sank.

sentences.zh: 虜悉眾圍之，矢下如雨。

translations.literal: The enemy surrounded them with their full force; arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy surrounded them with their full strength; arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 洪偽與虜和，圍少解。

translations.literal: Hong pretended to make peace with the enemy, and the siege loosened somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Hong pretended to make peace with the enemy, and the siege loosened somewhat.

sentences.zh: 洪率所領潰圍而出，死者大半，殺虜亦倍。

translations.literal: Hong led his men to break out; more than half died, but they also killed twice as many of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Hong led his men in breaking out of the encirclement; more than half perished, yet they also killed twice as many of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 洪及藥王除名為民，隆竟坐死。

translations.literal: Hong and Yaowang were stripped of rank and made commoners; Long was ultimately executed for his offense.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Yaowang were stripped of rank and reduced to commoners; Long was ultimately executed for his offense.

sentences.zh: 煬帝北巡，至恆安，見白骨被野，以問侍臣。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang toured the north and reached Heng'an; seeing white bones strewn across the fields, he asked his attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang toured the north and reached Heng'an; seeing white bones strewn across the countryside, he asked his attendants about it.

sentences.zh: 侍臣曰：「往者韓洪與虜戰處也。

translations.literal: The attendants said: "This is where Han Hong formerly fought the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants said, "This is where Han Hong once fought the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」帝憫然傷之，收葬骸骨，命五郡沙門為設佛供，拜洪隴西太守。

translations.literal: " The emperor was moved with pity, gathered and buried the bones, ordered Buddhist monks from five commanderies to offer Buddhist services, and appointed Hong Administrator of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was moved with pity, gathered and buried the bones, ordered Buddhist monks from five commanderies to offer Buddhist rites, and appointed Hong Administrator of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，硃崖民王萬昌作亂，詔洪擊平之。

translations.literal: Before long the people of Zhuyai, Wang Wanchang, rose in rebellion; an edict ordered Hong to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Wanchang of Zhuyai rebelled; an edict ordered Hong to attack and pacify him.

sentences.zh: 以功加位金紫光祿大夫，領郡如故。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Grand Master of Golden Brilliance with Imperial Approbation, continuing to head the commandery as before.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was advanced to Grand Master of Golden Brilliance with Imperial Approbation and continued to head the commandery as before.

sentences.zh: 俄而萬昌弟仲通複叛，又詔洪討平之。

translations.literal: Before long Wanchang's younger brother Zhongtong rebelled again, and again an edict ordered Hong to pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wanchang's younger brother Zhongtong rebelled again, and again an edict ordered Hong to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 師未旋，遇疾而卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: The army had not yet returned when he fell ill and died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army could return, he fell ill and died, at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: ○賀若弼

translations.literal: ○ He Ruobi
translations.idiomatic: ○ He Ruobi

sentences.zh: 賀若弼，字輔伯，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: He Ruobi, courtesy name Fubo, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi, whose courtesy name was Fubo, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父敦，以武烈知名，仕周為金州總管，宇文護忌而害之。

translations.literal: His father Dun was famed for martial valor, served the Zhou as Chief Administrator of Jin prefecture, and was killed by Yuwen Hu out of jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dun was renowned for martial prowess, served the Northern Zhou as Chief Administrator of Jin prefecture, and was killed by Yuwen Hu out of jealousy.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，呼弼謂之曰：「吾必欲平江南，然此心不果，汝當成吾志。

translations.literal: Facing execution, he called Bi and said to him: "I was determined to pacify Jiangnan, yet this heart's wish was not fulfilled—you must accomplish my aim.
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution, he called Bi to him and said, "I was determined to pacify Jiangnan, yet this wish went unfulfilled—you must accomplish what I could not.

sentences.zh: 且吾以舌死，汝不可不思。

translations.literal: Moreover, I die because of my tongue—you must not fail to reflect on this.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I die because of my tongue—you must not fail to take this to heart.

sentences.zh: 」因引錐刺弼舌出血，誡以慎口。

translations.literal: " With that he took an awl and pierced Bi's tongue until it bled, admonishing him to guard his speech.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he took an awl and pierced Bi's tongue until it bled, admonishing him to be careful with his words.

sentences.zh: 弼少慷慨有大志，驍勇便弓馬，解屬文，博涉書記，有重名於當世。

translations.literal: Bi from youth was generous-spirited with great ambition, fierce and brave and skilled with bow and horse, able to compose literary pieces, broadly versed in written records, and bore a weighty name in his age.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Bi was open-handed and ambitious, fierce in battle and skilled with bow and horse, able to compose literary pieces, widely read in books and records, and enjoyed a great reputation in his day.

sentences.zh: 周齊王憲聞而敬之，引為記室。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qi of the Zhou heard of him and treated him with respect, taking him on as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi of the Northern Zhou heard of him, treated him with respect, and took him on as recorder in his household.

sentences.zh: 未幾，封當亭縣公，遷小內史。

translations.literal: Before long he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dangting county and promoted to Junior Imperial Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dangting county and promoted to Junior Imperial Scribe.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，上柱國烏丸軌言於帝曰：「太子非帝王器，臣亦嘗與賀若弼論之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu of Zhou's time, Supreme Pillar of State Wuyuan Gui said to the emperor: "The crown prince lacks the makings of an emperor; your servant has also discussed this with He Ruobi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou, Supreme Pillar of State Wuyuan Gui said to the emperor, "The crown prince lacks the makings of an emperor; I have also discussed this with He Ruobi.

sentences.zh: 」帝呼弼問之，弼知太子不可動搖，恐禍及己，詭對曰：「皇太子德業日新，未睹其闕。

translations.literal: " The emperor summoned Bi and questioned him; Bi knew the crown prince could not be shaken, feared disaster for himself, and answered deceitfully: "The crown prince's virtue and achievement grow daily; I have not seen his faults.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor summoned Bi and questioned him. Bi knew the crown prince's position could not be shaken, feared harm to himself, and answered deceitfully, "The crown prince's virtue and achievement grow daily; I have not seen his faults.

sentences.zh: 」帝默然。

translations.literal: " The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 弼既退，軌讓其背己，弼曰：「君不密則失臣，臣不密則失身，所以不敢輕議也。

translations.literal: After Bi withdrew, Gui reproached him for betraying him; Bi said: "If the ruler is not discreet he loses his ministers; if the minister is not discreet he loses his life—therefore I dared not speak lightly.
translations.idiomatic: After Bi withdrew, Gui reproached him for betraying him. Bi said, "If the ruler is not discreet he loses his ministers; if the minister is not discreet he loses his life—that is why I dared not speak lightly.

sentences.zh: 」及宣帝嗣位，軌竟見誅，弼乃獲免。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, Gui was ultimately executed, and Bi thus escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, Gui was ultimately executed, and Bi thus escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 尋與韋孝寬伐陳，攻拔數十城，弼計居多。

translations.literal: Soon he joined Wei Xiaokuan in campaigning against Chen, storming and taking dozens of cities; Bi's plans predominated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined Wei Xiaokuan in campaigning against Chen, storming dozens of cities; Bi's plans accounted for most of their success.

sentences.zh: 拜夀州刺史，改封襄邑縣公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Shou prefecture and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Xiangyi county.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Shou prefecture and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Xiangyi county.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，尉迥作亂鄴城，恐弼為變，遣長孫平馳驛代之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was Chancellor, Yuwen Yong rebelled at Yecheng; fearing Bi might change sides, he sent Zhangsun Ping by post-horse relay to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu was Chancellor, Yuwen Yong rebelled at Yecheng; fearing Bi might turn against him, he sent Zhangsun Ping by relay horse to replace him.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，陰有並江南之志，訪可任者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he secretly harbored the aim of annexing Jiangnan and sought one fit for the task.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he secretly intended to annex Jiangnan and sought someone fit for the task.

sentences.zh: 高熲曰：「朝臣之內，文武才幹，無若賀若弼者。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong said: "Among the court ministers in civil and military talent and ability, none equals He Ruobi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong said, "Among the court ministers, in civil and military talent and ability, none equals He Ruobi.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「公得之矣。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "You have found the right man.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "You have found the right man.

sentences.zh: 」於是拜弼為吳州總管，委以平陳之事，弼忻然以為己任。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Bi was appointed Chief Administrator of Wu prefecture and entrusted with the task of pacifying Chen; Bi gladly took it as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Bi was appointed Chief Administrator of Wu prefecture and entrusted with the conquest of Chen; Bi gladly accepted it as his own mission.

sentences.zh: 與壽州總管源雄並為重鎮。

translations.literal: Together with Shou prefecture Chief Administrator Yuan Xiong he formed a pair of key strongpoints.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Yuan Xiong, Chief Administrator of Shou prefecture, he formed a pair of key strongpoints on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 弼遺雄詩曰：「交河驃騎幕，合浦伏波營，勿使騏驎上，無我二人名。」

translations.literal: Bi sent Xiong a poem saying: "The swift-cavalry camp at Jiaohe, the Fubo camp at Hepu—do not let it be said upon the qilin's back that our two names are absent."
translations.idiomatic: Bi sent Xiong a poem: "The swift-cavalry camp at Jiaohe, the Fubo camp at Hepu—let it not be said, when the qilin is mounted, that our two names are missing."

sentences.zh: 獻取陳十策，上稱善，賜以寶刀。

translations.literal: He presented ten stratagems for taking Chen; the emperor praised them and bestowed a precious saber.
translations.idiomatic: He presented ten stratagems for taking Chen; the emperor praised them and bestowed a precious saber on him.

sentences.zh: 開皇九年，大舉伐陳，以弼為行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaihuang a great campaign was launched against Chen, with Bi as campaigning commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaihuang a great campaign was launched against Chen, with Bi as campaigning commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 將渡江，酹酒而咒曰：「弼親承廟略，遠振國威，伐罪吊民，除凶翦暴，上天長江，鑒其若此。

translations.literal: About to cross the Yangzi, he poured a libation and swore: "Bi personally receives the court's grand design, displays the state's prestige afar, punishes the guilty and comforts the people, removes the vicious and cuts down the violent—Heaven and the Long River, witness that it is so.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to cross the Yangzi, he poured a libation and swore, "Bi personally receives the court's grand design, displays our state's might afar, punishes the guilty and comforts the people, removes the vicious and cuts down the violent—Heaven and the Long River, bear witness that it is so.

sentences.zh: 如便福善禍淫，大軍利涉；

translations.literal: If indeed fortune attends the good and calamity the wicked, the great army will cross in ease;
translations.idiomatic: If indeed fortune attends the good and calamity the wicked, the great army will cross with ease;

sentences.zh: 如事有乖違，得葬江魚腹中，死且不恨。

translations.literal: if matters go against this, let me be buried in the bellies of the river fish—I shall die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: if matters go against this, let me be buried in the bellies of the river fish—I shall die without regret.

sentences.zh: 」先是，弼請緣江防人每交代之際，必集曆陽。

translations.literal: " Earlier Bi had requested that whenever the river-guard troops changed shifts they must assemble at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier Bi had requested that whenever the river-guard troops changed shifts they must assemble at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 於是大列旗幟，營幕被野。

translations.literal: Thereupon he arrayed banners and flags in great numbers, and camp tents covered the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he arrayed banners and flags in great numbers, and camp tents covered the countryside.

sentences.zh: 陳人以為大兵至，悉發國中士馬。

translations.literal: The Chen believed a great army had arrived and mobilized all troops and horses in the state.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen believed a great army had arrived and mobilized all the troops and horses in the realm.

sentences.zh: 既知防人交代，其眾複散。

translations.literal: Once they learned it was only the guard troops changing shifts, their forces dispersed again.
translations.idiomatic: Once they learned it was only the guard troops changing shifts, their forces dispersed again.

sentences.zh: 後以為常，不復設備。

translations.literal: Later they took this as routine and no longer made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Later they took this as routine and no longer made preparations.

sentences.zh: 及此，弼以大軍濟江，陳人弗之覺也。

translations.literal: When this time came, Bi crossed the river with the great army, and the Chen did not detect it.
translations.idiomatic: When this time came, Bi crossed the river with the great army, and the Chen did not detect it.

sentences.zh: 襲陳南徐州，拔之，執其刺史黃恪。

translations.literal: He stormed Chen's southern Xuzhou, took it, and seized its governor Huang Ke.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Chen's southern Xuzhou, took it, and seized its governor, Huang Ke.

sentences.zh: 軍令嚴肅，秋毫不犯。

translations.literal: Military orders were strict; not even an autumn hair was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Military discipline was strict; not even the slightest harm was done to the people.

sentences.zh: 有軍士于民間沽酒者，弼立斬之。

translations.literal: When a soldier bought wine among the populace, Bi immediately beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When a soldier bought wine among the populace, Bi had him beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 進屯蔣山之白土岡，陳將魯達、周智安、任蠻奴、田瑞、樊毅、孔范、蕭摩訶等以勁兵拒戰。

translations.literal: He advanced and encamped at Baitu Hill on Mount Jiang; the Chen generals Lu Da, Zhou Zhian, Ren Mannu, Tian Rui, Fan Yi, Kong Fan, Xiao Mohe and others opposed him with crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and encamped at Baitu Hill on Mount Jiang; the Chen generals Lu Da, Zhou Zhian, Ren Mannu, Tian Rui, Fan Yi, Kong Fan, Xiao Mohe, and others opposed him with crack troops.

sentences.zh: 田瑞先犯弼軍，弼擊走之。

translations.literal: Tian Rui first attacked Bi's army; Bi struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rui attacked Bi's army first; Bi struck and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 魯達等相繼遞進，弼軍屢卻。

translations.literal: Lu Da and the others advanced in succession one after another, and Bi's army repeatedly fell back.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Da and the others advanced in succession, and Bi's army repeatedly fell back.

sentences.zh: 弼揣知其驕，士卒且惰，於是督厲將士，殊死戰，遂大破之。

translations.literal: Bi judged them arrogant and their troops already slack; he then urged his officers and soldiers on to fight to the death and utterly routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Bi judged them arrogant and their troops already slack; he then urged his officers and soldiers to fight to the death and utterly routed them.

sentences.zh: 麾下開府員明擒摩訶至，弼命左右牽斬之。

translations.literal: His subordinate Opening the Mansion Yuan Ming brought Mohe captive; Bi ordered attendants to drag him off for execution.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate Yuan Ming of Opening the Mansion rank brought Mohe captive; Bi ordered his attendants to drag him off for execution.

sentences.zh: 摩訶顏色自若，弼釋而禮之。

translations.literal: Mohe's countenance was calm as ever; Bi released him and treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe's expression remained calm as ever; Bi released him and treated him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 從北掖門而入。

translations.literal: He entered through the North Side Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He entered through the North Side Gate.

sentences.zh: 時韓擒虎已執陳叔寶，弼至，呼叔寶視之。

translations.literal: By then Han Qinhu had already seized Chen Shubao; when Bi arrived he called Shubao forth to look at him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Han Qinhu had already seized Chen Shubao; when Bi arrived he called Shubao forth to look at him.

sentences.zh: 叔寶惶懼流汗，股忄栗再拜。

translations.literal: Shubao was fearful and sweating; his thighs trembled as he bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao was fearful and sweating; his legs trembled as he bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 弼謂之曰：「小國之君，當大國卿，拜，禮也。

translations.literal: Bi said to him: "The ruler of a small state meeting a minister of a great state—bowing is proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said to him, "The ruler of a small state meeting a minister of a great state—bowing is proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 入朝不失作歸命侯，無勞恐懼。

translations.literal: On entering court you will not fail to be made Marquis Who Submits to the Mandate—no need for fear.
translations.idiomatic: When you enter court you will still be made Marquis Who Submits to the Mandate—there is no need for fear.

sentences.zh: 」既而弼恚恨不獲叔寶，功在韓擒虎之後，於是與擒虎相詢，挺刃而出。

translations.literal: " Soon Bi resented that he had not captured Shubao himself and that his merit ranked after Han Qinhu's; he then exchanged words with Qinhu and drew his blade to go forth.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Bi resented that he had not captured Shubao himself and that his merit ranked after Han Qinhu's; he then exchanged words with Qinhu and drew his blade.

sentences.zh: 上聞弼有功，大悅，下詔褒揚，語在《韓擒虎傳》。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of Bi's merit, was greatly pleased, and issued an edict of praise—the words are in the biography of Han Qinhu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of Bi's merit, was greatly pleased, and issued an edict of praise—the words are given in the biography of Han Qinhu.

sentences.zh: 晉王以弼先期決戰，違軍命，於是以弼屬吏。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin, because Bi had fought a decisive battle ahead of schedule in violation of military orders, handed him over to the judicial officers.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin, because Bi had fought a decisive battle ahead of schedule in violation of military orders, handed him over to the judicial officers.

sentences.zh: 上驛召之，及見，迎勞曰：」克定三吳，公之功也。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him by post-horse relay; when he arrived and was received, the emperor welcomed and comforted him, saying: "Pacifying the Three Wu is your achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him by relay horse; when he arrived, the emperor welcomed and comforted him, saying, "Pacifying the Three Wu is your achievement.

sentences.zh: 「命登禦坐，賜物八千段，加位上柱國，進爵宋國公，真食襄邑三千戶，加以寶劍、寶帶、金甕、金盤各一，並雉尾扇、曲蓋，雜彩二千段，女樂二部，又賜陳叔寶妹為妾。

translations.literal: " He ordered him to ascend the imperial seat, bestowed eight thousand lengths of goods, advanced him to Supreme Pillar of State, promoted him to Duke of the Song state, granted a substantive fief of three thousand households at Xiangyi, and in addition one each of precious sword, precious belt, golden jar and golden platter, together with pheasant-tail fans and curved canopy, two thousand lengths of mixed silks, two companies of female musicians, and also gave him Chen Shubao's younger sister as a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered him to take a seat on the imperial dais, bestowed eight thousand lengths of goods, advanced him to Supreme Pillar of State, promoted him to Duke of the Song state, granted a substantive fief of three thousand households at Xiangyi, and in addition one each of a precious sword, precious belt, golden jar, and golden platter, together with pheasant-tail fans and a curved canopy, two thousand lengths of mixed silks, two companies of female musicians, and Chen Shubao's younger sister as a concubine.

sentences.zh: 拜右領軍大將軍，尋轉右武候大將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Right Army of the Palace Guard, soon transferred to General of the Right Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of the Right Army of the Palace Guard and soon transferred to General of the Right Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 弼時貴盛，位望隆重，其兄隆為武都郡公，弟東為萬榮郡公，並刺史、列將。

translations.literal: Bi at that time was exalted and flourishing, his position and prestige weighty; his elder brother Long was Duke of Wudu commandery, his younger brother Dong Duke of Wanrong commandery—both governors and ranked generals.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Bi was at the height of honor and power; his elder brother Long was Duke of Wudu commandery and his younger brother Dong Duke of Wanrong commandery—both served as governors and ranked generals.

sentences.zh: 弼家珍玩不可勝計，婢妾曳綺羅者數百，時人榮之。

translations.literal: Bi's household treasures and curios were beyond counting; maidservants and concubines trailing brocades and gauzes numbered in the hundreds—men of the age envied him.
translations.idiomatic: The treasures and curios in Bi's household were beyond counting; maidservants and concubines trailing brocades and gauzes numbered in the hundreds—men of the age envied him.

sentences.zh: 弼自謂功名出朝臣之右，每以宰相自許。

translations.literal: Bi considered his merit and fame to surpass the court ministers and often regarded himself as fit for chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Bi considered his merit and fame to surpass the court ministers and often regarded himself as fit for chancellor.

sentences.zh: 既而楊素為右僕射，弼仍為將軍，甚不平，形於言色，由是免官，弼怨望愈甚。

translations.literal: Before long Yang Su became Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs while Bi remained a general; deeply resentful, he showed it in word and countenance; on this account he was dismissed from office, and Bi's resentment grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yang Su became Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs while Bi remained a general; deeply resentful, he showed it in word and countenance; on this account he was dismissed from office, and Bi's resentment grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 後數年，下弼獄，上謂之曰：「我以高熲、楊素為宰相，汝每倡言，雲此二人惟堪啖飯耳，是何意也？

translations.literal: Several years later Bi was cast into prison; the emperor said to him: "I made Gao Jiong and Yang Su chancellors, yet you repeatedly proclaimed that these two men were fit only for eating rice—what did you mean by this?
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Bi was cast into prison. The emperor said to him, "I made Gao Jiong and Yang Su chancellors, yet you repeatedly proclaimed that these two men were fit only for eating rice—what did you mean by that?

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「熲，臣之故人，素，臣之舅子，臣並知其為人，誠有此語。

translations.literal: " Bi said: "Jiong is your servant's old acquaintance; Su is your servant's nephew by marriage—I know both their characters, and truly I said this.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "Jiong is an old acquaintance of mine; Su is my nephew by marriage—I know both their characters, and I truly said this.

sentences.zh: 」公卿奏弼怨望，罪當死。

translations.literal: " The lords and ministers reported that Bi harbored resentment and that the crime merited death.
translations.idiomatic: " The lords and ministers reported that Bi harbored resentment and that the crime merited death.

sentences.zh: 上惜其功，於是除名為民。

translations.literal: The emperor valued his merit and therefore stripped him of rank and made him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued his merit and therefore stripped him of rank and reduced him to a commoner.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，複其爵位。

translations.literal: After more than a year his noble rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year his noble rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 上亦忌之，不復任使，然每宴賜，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor also grew wary of him and no longer employed him, yet at every feast he was rewarded and treated with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also grew wary of him and no longer employed him, yet at every feast he was rewarded and treated with great generosity.

sentences.zh: 開皇十九年，上幸仁壽宮，宴王公，詔弼為五言詩，詞意憤怨，帝覽而容之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kaihuang the emperor visited Renshou Palace and feasted the princes and dukes; he ordered Bi to compose a five-character poem; its words were resentful and bitter, yet the emperor read it and bore with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Kaihuang the emperor visited Renshou Palace and feasted the princes and dukes; he ordered Bi to compose a five-character poem; its words were resentful and bitter, yet the emperor read it and bore with him.

sentences.zh: 嘗遇突厥入朝，上賜之射，突厥一發中的。

translations.literal: Once when Turks came to court the emperor granted them an archery contest; a Turk hit the target with one shot.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Turks came to court the emperor granted them an archery contest; a Turk hit the target with one shot.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「非賀若弼無能當此。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Apart from He Ruobi no one can match this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Apart from He Ruobi no one can match this.

sentences.zh: 」於是命弼。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Bi.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered Bi to shoot.

sentences.zh: 弼再拜祝曰：「臣若赤誠奉國者，當一發破的。

translations.literal: Bi bowed twice and prayed: "If your servant serves the state with loyal sincerity, let one shot strike the target.
translations.idiomatic: Bi bowed twice and prayed, "If I serve the state with loyal sincerity, let one shot strike the target.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，發不中也。

translations.literal: If not so, let the shot miss.
translations.idiomatic: If not, let the shot miss.

sentences.zh: 」既射，一發而中。

translations.literal: " He shot, and with one arrow hit the target.
translations.idiomatic: " He shot, and with one arrow hit the target.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，顧謂突厥曰：「此人天賜我也！」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and, turning to the Turks, said: "This man Heaven has given to me!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and, turning to the Turks, said, "This man Heaven has given to me!"

sentences.zh: 煬帝之在東宮，嘗謂弼曰：「楊素、韓擒虎、史萬歲三人，俱稱良將，優劣如何？

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was in the Eastern Palace he once said to Bi: "Yang Su, Han Qinhu and Shi Wansui—three men all called fine generals—how do they rank in merit?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang was crown prince he once said to Bi, "Yang Su, Han Qinhu, and Shi Wansui are all called fine generals—how do they compare?

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「楊素是猛將，非謀將；

translations.literal: " Bi said: "Yang Su is a fierce general, not a strategist;
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "Yang Su is a fierce general, not a strategist;

sentences.zh: 韓擒虎是鬥將，非領將；

translations.literal: Han Qinhu is a combat general, not a commanding general;
translations.idiomatic: Han Qinhu is a combat general, not a commanding general;

sentences.zh: 史萬歲是騎將，非大將。

translations.literal: Shi Wansui is a cavalry general, not a great general.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wansui is a cavalry general, not a great general.

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「然則大將誰也？

translations.literal: " The crown prince said: "Then who is the great general?
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince said, "Then who is the great general?

sentences.zh: 」弼拜曰：「唯殿下所擇。

translations.literal: " Bi bowed and said: "Whomever Your Highness chooses.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi bowed and said, "Whomever Your Highness chooses."

sentences.zh: 」弼意自許為大將。

translations.literal: " Bi in his mind regarded himself as the great general.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi took himself to be the great general.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝嗣位，尤被疏忌。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Bi was especially kept at a distance and viewed with suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Bi was especially kept at a distance and viewed with suspicion.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，從駕北巡，至榆林。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye he accompanied the emperor on the northern tour to Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye he accompanied the emperor on the northern tour as far as Yulin.

sentences.zh: 帝時為大帳，其下可坐數千人，召突厥啟民可汗饗之。

translations.literal: The emperor at that time had a great tent beneath which several thousand could be seated; he summoned the Turkic Qaghan Qimin for a feast.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at that time pitched a great tent beneath which several thousand could be seated, and summoned the Turkic qaghan Qimin to feast there.

sentences.zh: 弼以為大侈，與高熲、宇文弼等私議得失，為人所奏，竟坐誅，時年六十四。

translations.literal: Bi considered this extravagantly excessive; he privately discussed its faults with Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi and others; someone reported them, and he was ultimately executed for the offense, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Bi considered this extravagantly excessive; he privately discussed its faults with Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and others; someone reported them, and he was ultimately executed for the offense, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 妻子為官奴婢，群從徙邊。

translations.literal: His wife and children were made government slave-girls and servants; his clan kin were banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children were made government slaves; his clan kin were banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 子懷亮，慷慨有父風，以柱國世子拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: His son Huailiang was generous-spirited with his father's manner; as heir of a Pillar of State he was appointed Senior General-in-Chief of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huailiang was generous-spirited and had his father's manner; as heir of a Pillar of State he was appointed Senior General-in-Chief of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 坐弼為奴，俄亦誅死。

translations.literal: Because Bi was made a slave, he too was soon executed.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Bi's disgrace as a slave, he too was soon executed.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫天地未泰，聖哲啟其機；

translations.literal: The historian says: When heaven and earth are not yet at peace, sage rulers open the mechanism;
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: When heaven and earth are not yet at peace, sage rulers open the way forward;

sentences.zh: 疆埸尚梗，爪牙宣其力。

translations.literal: when the frontier still obstructs, claw and fang display their strength.
translations.idiomatic: when the frontier still blocks the way, generals display their strength.

sentences.zh: 周之方、邵，漢室韓、彭，代有其人，非一時也。

translations.literal: Fang and Shao of Zhou, Han Xin and Peng Yue of the Han house—each age has had such men, not only one period.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and Shao of the Zhou, Han Xin and Peng Yue of the Han—each age has had such men; they do not belong to one time alone.

sentences.zh: 自晉衰微，中原幅裂，區宇分隔，將三百年。

translations.literal: From the decline of Jin the Central Plains were rent asunder; the realm was divided for nearly three hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: From the decline of Jin the Central Plains were torn apart; the realm remained divided for nearly three hundred years.

sentences.zh: 陳氏憑長江之地險，恃金陵之餘氣，以為天限南北，人莫能窺。

translations.literal: The Chen relied on the Yangzi's geographic advantage and Jinling's lingering vitality, thinking heaven had set north and south as limits that no man could penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen relied on the Yangzi's strategic terrain and Jinling's lingering prestige, believing heaven had set north and south as a boundary no man could cross.

sentences.zh: 高祖爰應千齡，將一函夏。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu in response to a thousand-year destiny was about to unite all within the Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu, answering a thousand-year destiny, was about to unite all within the realm.

sentences.zh: 賀若弼慷慨，申必取之長策，韓擒虎奮發，賈餘勇以爭先，勢甚疾雷，鋒逾駭電。

translations.literal: He Ruobi was generous-spirited and set forth the long-term strategy that must take Chen; Han Qinhu roused himself and sold his remaining courage to strive ahead—the momentum like swift thunder, the edge surpassing startling lightning.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi, open-handed and bold, set forth the long-term strategy that must take Chen; Han Qinhu roused himself and pressed on with his remaining strength—their momentum like swift thunder, their edge surpassing startling lightning.

sentences.zh: 隋氏自此一戎，威加四海。

translations.literal: From this one campaign the Sui thereby extended their might across the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: With this one campaign the Sui extended their might across the four seas.

sentences.zh: 稽諸天道，或時有廢興，考之人謀，實二臣之力。

translations.literal: When examined against heaven's way, at times there is decline and rise; when examined against human planning, it was truly the merit of these two ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When measured against heaven's way, at times there is decline and rise; when measured against human planning, it was truly the achievement of these two ministers.

sentences.zh: 其俶儻英略，賀若居多，武毅威雄，韓擒虎稱重。

translations.literal: In dashing talent and heroic strategy He Ruobi predominates; in martial fierceness and awesome might Han Qinhu is weighed the heavier.
translations.idiomatic: In bold talent and heroic strategy He Ruobi predominates; in martial fierceness and imposing might Han Qinhu carries the greater weight.

sentences.zh: 方于晉之王、杜，勳庸綽有餘地。

translations.literal: Compared with Wang and Du of Jin, their achievements leave ample room beyond.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Wang Hun and Du Yu of Jin, their achievements leave ample room beyond.

sentences.zh: 然賀若功成名立，矜伐不已，竟顛殞於非命，亦不密以失身。

translations.literal: Yet He Ruobi, merit and fame established, kept boasting without end and ultimately fell to an untimely death—failing to keep his speech discreet cost him his life.
translations.idiomatic: Yet He Ruobi, once merit and fame were established, kept boasting without end and ultimately fell to an untimely death—failing to guard his speech cost him his life.

sentences.zh: 若念父臨終之言，必不及於斯禍矣。

translations.literal: Had he kept in mind his father's dying words, he would surely not have reached this disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Had he kept in mind his father's dying words, he would surely not have met this disaster.

sentences.zh: 韓擒虎累世將家，威聲動俗，敵國既破，名遂身全，幸也。

translations.literal: Han Qinhu came from generations of military houses; his martial renown shook the age; the enemy state once broken, his fame complete and person intact—he was fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qinhu came from generations of military houses; his martial renown shook the age; once the enemy state was broken, his fame was complete and his person intact—he was fortunate.

sentences.zh: 廣陵、甘棠，鹹有武藝，驍雄膽略，並為當時所推，赳赳干城，難兄難弟矣。

translations.literal: The houses of Guangling and Gantang alike possessed martial arts; fierce and brave in strategy and courage, all were praised in their day—in guarding the realm as staunch brothers, who could match them?
translations.idiomatic: The lines of Guangling and Gantang alike possessed martial skill; fierce in battle and bold in strategy, all were praised in their day—as staunch guardians of the realm, they were brothers without peer.
